newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures shrug off gloom to end higher.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures shrug off gloom to end higher.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures shrugged aside their recent gloom to end higher for the first time in four days as bargain-hunting in blue-chip counters buoyed the underlying cash market, dealers said on Tuesday.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract gained 485 points to close at 17,820 after trading in a volatile 660-points range.
"Everybody was waiting for 17,800 to sell the market. But when it came, it looked so strong that they just held back," said a trader with a local futures house.
"Today's close was good and if we can close above 18,000 next, we can say goodbye to the downtrend for a while," he said.
He said the market could enter a consolidation phase in the short-term if it managed to sustain gains above 17,500.
But dealers said the longer-term trend remained bearish as there was no change in Japan's economic fundamentals.
"For the market to really recover, we'd need to see 19,750 and that's still far away," the trader added.

Nikkei cash and futures markets came under pressure on Monday on fresh anxieties about Japan's financial sector following Moody's downgrade of four banks and rumours a Japanese bank had posted major losses in derivatives trading.
The March MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 307.7 against its opening 307.5 on volume of 300 lots.
